column4: 他的儿女都在国外工作。
column5: His children all work abroad.
column6: 儿女 means sons and daughters, usually when talking about someone's grown-up children. 孩子 is any child.

column4: 这是一辆二手车，很便宜。
column5: This is a second-hand car, and it is very cheap.
column6: 二手 comes before a noun: 二手车, 二手书. 二 is "second" and 手 is "hand".

column4: 用手机扫一下二维码，就可以付钱。
column5: Scan the QR code with your phone and you can pay.
column6: 二维码 is a QR code. 扫二维码 means to scan one. 二维 means "two-dimensional" and 码 means "code".

column4: 他在报纸上发表了一篇文章。
column5: He published an article in the newspaper.
column6: 发表 is to publish a piece of writing, or to state an opinion in public: 发表意见.

column4: 公司明天发布新手机。
column5: The company will release a new phone tomorrow.
column6: 发布 is to make something public in an official way: 发布消息 (to release news), 发布通知 (to issue a notice).

column4: 这个国家的经济很发达。
column5: This country's economy is very developed.
column6: 发达 describes a country, region or business that has developed well: 发达国家 (a developed country).

column3: to bring into play; to perform
column4: 他昨天在比赛中发挥得很好。
column5: He performed very well in the match yesterday.
column6: 发挥 is to let your ability or a thing show its power: 发挥作用 (to play a role), 发挥得很好 (to perform well).

column4: 谁发明了电话？
column5: Who invented the telephone?
column6: 发明 is to make something that did not exist before. As a noun it is "an invention".

column4: 这个活动是他发起的。
column5: He launched this activity.
column6: 发起 is to be the first to start an event or campaign: 发起活动. 发起人 is the person who started it.

column3: to speak (at a meeting); a speech
column4: 在会上，他第一个发言了。
column5: At the meeting, he was the first to speak.
column6: 发言 is to speak formally in a meeting or a discussion. As a noun it is a speech or statement.

column4: 他的汉语发音很好。
column5: His Chinese pronunciation is very good.
column6: 发音 is how you pronounce sounds. It is also a verb, "to pronounce". 读音 is the reading of a character in the dictionary.

column4: 开车超速要罚钱。
column5: You will be fined for speeding.
column6: 罚 is to make someone pay or suffer for breaking a rule: 罚钱 (to fine), 罚站 (to make someone stand as a punishment).

column4: 他开车超速，被罚款了。
column5: He was fined for speeding.
column6: 罚款 is a verb plus object (to fine someone) and also a noun (a fine).

column4: 这件事要去法院解决。
column5: This matter must be settled in court.
column6: 法院 is the court where a judge decides a case.

column3: to turn over; to flip; to translate
column4: 请翻到第十页。
column5: Please turn to page ten.
column6: 翻 is to turn something over: 翻书 (to turn the pages), 翻身 (to turn over). It also means to translate (翻译) or to climb over (翻墙).

column4: 我喜欢吃番茄炒鸡蛋。
column5: I like eating stir-fried tomatoes with eggs.
column6: 番茄 is the tomato. People also say 西红柿 in speech.

column4: 这个城市越来越繁荣。
column5: This city is getting more and more prosperous.
column6: 繁荣 is for a city, an economy or a culture that is doing well: 经济繁荣.

column3: opposite; reversed; the wrong way round
column4: 你把衣服穿反了。
column5: You have put your clothes on the wrong way round.
column6: 反 means "the other way round" (反方向 = the opposite direction). It is also in 反对 (to oppose) and 相反 (opposite).

column4: 下雨以后，天气没有变凉，反而更热了。
column5: After the rain the weather did not get cooler; on the contrary, it got hotter.
column6: 反而 shows a result that is the opposite of what you would expect. It often follows a clause with 不 or 没.

column4: 他反复看这封信，还是看不懂。
column5: He reads the letter again and again but still cannot understand it.
column6: 反复 comes before a verb: 反复练习 (to practise repeatedly). As a noun it can also mean a setback or relapse (病情有反复).

column4: 请返回你的座位。
column5: Please return to your seat.
column6: 返回 is a formal word for going back to a place: 返回学校, 返回座位. 回 is the everyday word.

column4: 他对这个消息没有什么反应。
column5: He has no reaction to this news.
column6: 反应 is how someone or something responds: 有反应 (to react), 没有反应 (no reaction). Do not mix it up with 反映, which sounds the same.

column4: 这个电影反映真实的生活。
column5: This film reflects real life.
column6: 反映 is to show or to report something: 反映生活 (to reflect life), 反映问题 (to report a problem to someone above). It sounds the same as 反应 (fǎnyìng).

column4: 反正我没有事，我和你一起去。
column5: Anyway, I have nothing to do, so I will go with you.
column6: 反正 means "whatever happens, it is the same": 反正都一样 (it is all the same anyway).

column4: 这次考试的范围很大。
column5: The scope of this exam is very wide.
column6: 范围 is the limit of an area, topic or activity: 考试范围 (the scope of an exam), 在……范围内 (within the scope of).

column4: 这张桌子是方的。
column5: This table is square.
column6: 方 means "square" (方的) and also a side or direction: 东方 (the east), 方向 (direction), 双方 (both sides).

column4: 经理让我们做一个新方案。
column5: The manager asks us to make a new plan.
column6: 方案 is a detailed plan for solving a problem or doing a job: 工作方案. 计划 is the general word for a plan.

column4: 冬天要多穿衣服，防感冒。
column5: In winter you need to wear more clothes to guard against colds.
column6: 防 is to take care against something bad: 防火, 防雨, 防感冒.

column4: 这个地区的房屋都很新。
column5: The houses in this area are all new.
column6: 房屋 is a written word for buildings where people live. 房子 is the spoken word.

column4: 我们要防止孩子玩火。
column5: We must prevent children from playing with fire.
column6: 防止 is to stop something bad before it happens: 防止事故 (prevent accidents), 防止浪费 (prevent waste).

column4: 天气很热，仿佛回到了夏天。
column5: It is so hot, as if summer has come back.
column6: 仿佛 is "as if" in written style. 仿佛……一样 means "just as if".

column4: 校长明年要访问中国。
column5: The head teacher will visit China next year.
column6: 访问 is a formal visit to a person, a place or a country. It also means to interview someone, and to visit a website (访问网站).

column4: 飞机飞行了五个小时。
column5: The plane flew for five hours.
column6: 飞行 is flying by aircraft or spaceship: 飞行员 (pilot), 飞行时间 (flight time).

column4: 他想当一名飞行员。
column5: He wants to be a pilot.
column6: 飞行员 is a pilot. 员 is a person who does a job, as in 服务员 (waiter).

column4: 他去过很多非洲国家。
column5: He has been to many African countries.
column6: 非洲 is Africa. 洲 means a continent: 亚洲 (Asia), 欧洲 (Europe).

column4: 大家分别回到了自己的家。
column5: Everyone went back to their own home separately.
column6: 分别 as an adverb comes before a verb. As a verb it means to part (我们在车站分别), and as a noun a difference (没有分别).

column3: to be distributed; to be spread
column4: 这种树分布在南方。
column5: This kind of tree is distributed in the south.
column6: 分布 is how things are spread over an area: 分布在 + place.

column3: one after another; in great numbers
column4: 听到消息，大家纷纷来了。
column5: After hearing the news, everyone came one after another.
column6: 纷纷 comes before a verb and shows many people or things doing something one after another: 纷纷离开.

column4: 请把垃圾分类。
column5: Please sort the rubbish.
column6: 分类 is a verb plus object. 垃圾分类 means sorting rubbish into kinds.

column4: 孩子不想和妈妈分离。
column5: The child does not want to be separated from mum.
column6: 分离 is to come apart or be apart: 和……分离. 分开 is the everyday word.

column4: 老师把工作分配给了大家。
column5: The teacher assigned the work to everyone.
column6: 分配 is to divide things or tasks and give each person a share: 分配工作, 分配时间.

column3: to break up; to part ways
column4: 他们去年分手了。
column5: They broke up last year.
column6: 分手 is to end a relationship, or to say goodbye at a crossing. It is a verb plus object: 分了手, 和他分手.

column4: 我们来分析一下这个问题。
column5: Let us analyse this problem.
column6: 分析 is to break a problem into parts and study them: 分析原因 (to analyse the reason).

column4: 我想和大家分享一个好消息。
column5: I want to share some good news with everyone.
column6: 分享 is to share something with others, such as news, happiness or an experience.

column3: to strive; to struggle for a goal
column4: 他为自己的梦想奋斗了十年。
column5: He has struggled for his dream for ten years.
column6: 奋斗 is to work hard for a goal for a long time: 为……奋斗.

column4: 学校的生活丰富多彩。
column5: School life is rich and colourful.
column6: 丰富多彩 is a four-character expression: 丰富 (rich) plus 多彩 (many colours). It praises a life or an event full of variety.

column4: 这个歌手的风格很特别。
column5: This singer's style is very special.
column6: 风格 is the way an artist, a writer or a designer does things: 写作风格 (writing style).

column4: 球迷们疯狂地喊着他的名字。
column5: The fans are shouting his name wildly.
column6: 疯狂 describes wild, uncontrolled behaviour, or something very strong: 疯狂购物.

column4: 每个地方都有不同的风俗。
column5: Every place has different customs.
column6: 风俗 is a custom that belongs to a place or a people. 风俗习惯 is also common.

column4: 做生意有风险。
column5: Doing business has risks.
column6: 风险 is a chance of loss or danger: 有风险 (there is a risk), 冒风险 (to take a risk).

column4: 他否定了这个办法，因为太贵。
column5: He rejected this method because it was too expensive.
column6: 否定 is to say no to an idea or plan. As an adjective it means "negative", and 否定句 is a negative sentence.

column4: 他否认自己做过这件事。
column5: He denies that he has done this.
column6: 否认 is to say that something is not true, such as a fact or an accusation. Its opposite is 承认 (to admit).

column4: 这对夫妇有两个孩子。
column5: This married couple has two children.
column6: 夫妇 is a husband and wife together. Its measure word is 对: 一对夫妇.

column3: to support with the hand; to help up
column4: 他扶着老人过马路。
column5: He helps the old man across the road, holding him.
column6: 扶 is to hold someone or something to keep it steady: 扶老人 (to help an old person), 扶起来 (to help up).

column4: 过年的时候，家家门上都贴福字。
column5: At New Year, every home sticks a character for good fortune on the door.
column6: 福 means good fortune, as in 幸福 (happy) and 福气 (good luck). At New Year people often hang the character 福.

column4: 这家店的服装很有特色。
column5: The clothes in this shop are very distinctive.
column6: 服装 is a general, formal word for clothes, especially fashion and costumes: 服装店. 衣服 is the everyday word.

column4: 我买了一副新眼镜。
column5: I bought a new pair of glasses.
column6: 副 counts things that come as a pair or a set: 一副眼镜. It also means "deputy": 副经理.

column4: 这个地方很富，家家都有汽车。
column5: This place is very rich, and every family has a car.
column6: 富 is rich in money or resources. Its opposite is 穷 (poor).

column3: to pay; to put in (effort, time or money)
column4: 他为这个家付出了很多。
column5: He has paid a lot for this family.
column6: 付出 is to give effort, time, money or feelings: 付出努力 (to put in effort), 付出时间 (to give time).

column4: 这笔钱我可以负担。
column5: I can bear this sum of money.
column6: 负担 as a verb is to carry a cost. As a noun it is a burden: 减轻负担 (to lighten the load).

column4: 妇女和男人一样可以工作。
column5: Women can work just like men.
column6: 妇女 is a formal word for adult women. In speech people say 女人.

column4: 这位老师富有爱心。
column5: This teacher is rich in compassion.
column6: 富有 means "rich in" something: 富有爱心 (full of care), 富有经验 (rich in experience). It can also mean "wealthy".

column4: 请把这个文件复制到电脑里。
column5: Please copy this file to the computer.
column6: 复制 is to make an exact copy of a file, text or picture: 复制文件.

column4: 学校改革了考试的办法。
column5: The school reformed its way of examining.
column6: 改革 is a big change to fix a system: 教育改革 (education reform).

column4: 这个办法还需要改进。
column5: This method still needs improving.
column6: 改进 is to make a method, a product or work better: 改进办法. 改善 is for conditions.

column4: 这里的生活条件已经改善了很多。
column5: Living conditions here have improved a lot.
column6: 改善 makes a situation better: 改善生活 (to improve living standards), 改善关系 (to improve a relationship).

column4: 我们改天再见吧。
column5: Let us meet another day.
column6: 改天 means "some other day" and is often used to put off a plan: 改天再说 (let us talk about it another day).

column4: 老师让他改正了作业里的错误。
column5: The teacher asked him to correct the mistakes in his homework.
column6: 改正 is to fix a mistake or a bad habit: 改正错误, 改正习惯.

column4: 他们在山下盖了一座新房子。
column5: They built a new house at the foot of the hill.
column6: 盖 means to build a house (盖房子), to put something over (盖被子), and as a noun it is a lid (盖子).

column4: 请你概括一下这篇文章的意思。
column5: Please sum up the meaning of this article.
column6: 概括 is to give the main points in a short form: 概括内容 (to sum up the content).

column4: 这个概念很难懂。
column5: This concept is hard to understand.
column6: 概念 is a general idea of something in the mind: 时间概念 (a sense of time).

column3: to dare to; to have the courage to
column4: 他敢于说出自己的想法。
column5: He dares to speak his mind.
column6: 敢于 + verb means "to have the courage to do". It is a written, positive word: 敢于尝试 (to dare to try). 敢 is the everyday word.

column4: 我到车站的时候，公共汽车刚好来了。
column5: When I arrived at the station, the bus came just in time.
column6: 刚好 means "at just the right moment or amount": 刚好够 (just enough).

column4: 他长得很高大。
column5: He is tall and big.
column6: 高大 is for tall, strong people and for big things such as trees and buildings: 高大的树.

column4: 这家高档饭馆很贵。
column5: This high-end restaurant is very expensive.
column6: 高档 means high class: 高档商品 (high-end goods). Its opposite is 低档.

column4: 这座楼的高度是二十米。
column5: The height of this building is twenty metres.
column6: 高度 is the height of something. As an adverb it means "highly": 高度重视 (to attach great importance to).
